version.description: The installed version this finding is about. OPTIONAL since P1-A5, and omitted only when the instance's own version could not be established at all -- a private, versionless workspace package is the genuine case. It is never borrowed from a sibling instance of the same name and never filled with a sentinel. This relaxation is additive: an instance with no version previously produced no finding whatsoever, so no finding that carried a version before P1-A5 stopped carrying one.

packageInstance.description: WHICH installed instance this finding is about (P1-A5). Project-relative POSIX path when the instance lives inside the scanned project (e.g. "node_modules/foo" vs "packages/app/node_modules/foo"), canonical absolute path otherwise (a pnpm store, an npm-linked checkout). Two findings sharing an advisory id, a package name and a version but naming different instances are two independent verdicts about two different physical installs -- one may be AFFECTED while the other is NOT_AFFECTED -- and this field is what makes them distinguishable. Presentation only: it is derived from the canonical PackageInstanceId that identity comparisons actually use, and must not be parsed back into one.

confirmedAbsentFromModuleLoadClosure.description: VT-307d module-load absence proof: positive evidence that this exact canonical installed package instance cannot be loaded from the configured entrypoint roots, under VulnTrace's declared supported module-loading model. Present only on a NOT_AFFECTED whose reasons include package_instance_not_in_complete_module_load_closure. This is module-load absence, NOT call-graph absence.

packageInstance.description: The exact canonical install LOCATION proved absent -- never a package name, version, or name+version pair.

entrypointRoots.description: The configured entrypoint files the absence proof is relative to. Non-empty by construction.

closureComplete.description: Always true: closure completeness is the load-bearing precondition, recorded explicitly rather than left implicit.

confirmedAbsentInstance.description: VT-307e proof family B (hardened by VT-307e's own final audit): positive evidence that this exact canonical installed package instance was never traversed by a non-truncated call graph, AND is independently corroborated absent from a complete, gate-eligible ModuleLoadClosure. Call-graph absence alone (graphTruncated=false) is NOT sufficient -- a package instance reached only through a re-export declaration is invisible to call-graph discovery while genuinely loaded and called, so the ModuleLoadClosure corroboration is the load-bearing half of this proof. Distinct from confirmedAbsentFromModuleLoadClosure, which is the stronger claim that the instance cannot be LOADED at all, established directly rather than by corroboration.

packageInstance.description: Exact canonical install LOCATION -- never a name or version.

entrypointRoots.description: The configured entrypoint files this proof is relative to. Non-empty by construction.

graphTruncated.description: Always false: a truncated call graph cannot support this proof (VT-202). Establishes only that the call graph's traversal did not hit a resource limit -- not that the call graph is complete.

moduleLoadClosureComplete.description: Always true: the independent ModuleLoadClosure corroboration that makes this proof sound despite the call graph's own traversal not being import-complete (VT-307e).

confirmedUnreachableTarget.description: VT-307e proof family C: positive evidence that a resolved, attributed vulnerable target has no call path from any configured entrypoint, established by an exhaustive search that met no unresolved edge in the reachable subgraph. Says nothing about whether the package is present or loaded -- it may be both. VT-CONTRACT-02 renamed this proof's completeness field from callGraphComplete to reachableSubgraphComplete: the old name asserted a property of the WHOLE call graph that this proof never established, and a consumer could reasonably have read it as a stronger claim than the analyzer makes. Family B's identical field was retired by VT-307e for the identical reason.

entrypointRoots.description: The configured entrypoint files this proof is relative to. Non-empty by construction.

reachableSubgraphComplete.description: Always true, and the narrowest accurate statement of what this proof rests on: the REACHABLE SUBGRAPH -- the nodes analyzeReachability reaches from the entrypoint source node over resolved edges -- was enumerated to exhaustion AND contained no unresolved edge anywhere in it. Both halves are load-bearing: analyzeReachability returns `unreachable` only when it drains its queue and met no unresolved edge, and returns `unknown` otherwise, so this is not merely 'the search finished'. Scoped to that subgraph and no further: NOT a claim that the call graph is complete, that the package is unloaded, or that unresolved edges elsewhere in the program do not exist. The separate graphTruncated === false requirement (VT-202) is enforced by buildFinding ahead of this proof.

unknownReasons.description: FOUNDATION F3. Why this finding is UNKNOWN, machine-readably. Present on UNKNOWN findings and on no others: an AFFECTED carries a reproduced path and a NOT_AFFECTED carries a positive proof, so neither is uncertain and neither may carry this. Purely OBSERVATIONAL -- every entry is derived from the same blockers the verdict rules already acted on, after those rules ran, and removing the field would change no verdict anywhere. It does not replace evidence.reasons, which is retained verbatim and carries the specifics (which module, which file and line) that a token cannot. Entries are deduplicated by (category, reason) and ordered by the taxonomy's own declaration order -- never by count and never by observation order -- so the array is byte-stable across runs.

category.description: The KIND OF WORK this uncertainty represents. unmodeled_construct: a construct the analyzer saw and has not implemented (closeable by frontend work). value_uncertainty: the construct is modeled but the value or destination is not statically unique. capability_escape: the runtime can reach outside bounded static reasoning (eval, dynamic loading, loader mutation) -- largely not closeable. identity_unresolved: a package/instance/version/entry/target identity fact was never established. analysis_precondition_unmet: something the decision depends on was never established at all (unparseable source, no runtime implementation, no vulnerable-symbol rule, no module-load closure). budget_exceeded: a configured bound stopped the work.

reason.description: The specific reason, one level below category. Every DynamicCallReason appears verbatim, so a token here is the same string the diagnostics prose names. This enum grows ADDITIVELY: P1-B1 added the eight unsupported_* subtypes that decompose unsupported_construct into the specific frontend modeling gap behind each occurrence, and retained unsupported_construct itself as their runtime floor, so no previously emitted token was removed or given a new meaning. All nine share the unmodeled_construct category, so a consumer aggregating by category is unaffected; a consumer matching the exact string unsupported_construct will now see fewer of them and should match the unsupported_ prefix, or aggregate by category, instead.

count.description: Occurrences observed for this exact (category, reason) pair. A reachability search over a real package produces hundreds of unresolved edges carrying a handful of distinct reasons; this is what lets a consumer see 47 x unsupported_construct rather than 47 rows.

allOf.description: VT-CONTRACT-01 -- EXACTLY ONE negative proof on a NOT_AFFECTED. NOT_AFFECTED is a positive claim (see src/domain/evidence.ts's negative-proof contract), so a NOT_AFFECTED finding must carry precisely one of the three proof-family evidence objects: never zero (an unproven NOT_AFFECTED is exactly the false negative AGENTS.md forbids), and never two or more (the three families make materially different claims under different preconditions, so a finding asserting more than one is contradictory about what was actually established). oneOf expresses EXACTLY one rather than at least one: each branch requires a different proof object, so a finding carrying two matches two branches and is rejected. `required: [evidence]` is restated here, rather than inherited from the sibling if/then above, so this invariant cannot be silently weakened by a later edit to that rule.

oneOf.title: Family B -- exact-instance absence corroborated by call graph and module-load closure

allOf.description: VT-CONTRACT-01 -- NO negative proof on any other verdict. The three proof objects justify NOT_AFFECTED and nothing else: an AFFECTED carrying one would assert a reachable path and its own absence simultaneously, and an UNKNOWN carrying one would present a completed proof for a verdict that exists precisely because no proof completed. Stated as three false subschemas rather than one `not`, so a violation reports the exact offending field. This is what stops stale proof evidence from surviving an accidental object reuse or a future refactor.

unreportedCandidates.description: FOUNDATION F3. Vulnerability candidates that produced NO finding row, each with why. NOT FINDINGS: no verdict, no evidence, no confidence, a separate array, and no code path converts one into a finding. Before F3 every one of these states was either invisible or a line of English on stderr, so a confident 'this advisory does not apply to this instance' and 'this scan never considered that instance' reached a consumer as identical bytes. OPTIONAL in this schema so that results produced before F3 remain valid; always emitted, possibly empty, by every scan since. Ordered by (stage, package, packageInstance, vulnerability, reason, detail) so the array is a function of what was unreported, never of enumeration order.

stage.description: Where in the pipeline the candidate stopped, widest to narrowest. workspace_discovery: an unknown NUMBER of candidates may never have been enumerated, so no package is named. package_identity: a known instance could not be placed against advisory ranges. advisory_applicability: a known instance was evaluated against a known advisory.

disposition.description: Whether the absence of a finding is a CONCLUSION or a GAP, and the most important field here. not_applicable: VulnTrace positively established that the advisory does not apply -- the installed version is outside every affected range. That is real information arrived at with certainty and is NOT uncertainty; it carries no category and must never be counted as an analysis gap. It is equally NOT a NOT_AFFECTED verdict: it is a statement about version ranges only, no reachability analysis ran, and no negative proof exists. undetermined: applicability could not be established, so nothing is claimed either way.

vulnerability.description: The advisory this entry is about, when one was known.

package.description: The package name, when one was known. Absent on a workspace_discovery entry, where what is missing is exactly the set of packages nobody enumerated.

packageInstance.description: The exact installed instance, rendered as in a finding's packageInstance: project-relative POSIX path inside the scanned project, canonical absolute path otherwise. Presentation only; never parsed back into an identity.

version.description: The installed version, when it was established. Omitted rather than defaulted, for the same reason a finding's version is.

reason.description: The specific reason, from the same vocabulary unknownReasons uses -- one token namespace, not two -- plus advisory_not_applicable_to_installed_version, which is deliberately NOT an uncertainty reason: it has no category, can never appear in unknownReasons, and so cannot be aggregated into an uncertainty count by mistake.

category.description: The uncertainty class, present IF AND ONLY IF disposition is undetermined. Its absence on a not_applicable entry is structural: a confident non-applicability has no uncertainty class because it is not uncertain.

detail.description: Human-readable explanation; always present. Where the same condition also appears in diagnostics, this is the same sentence, so the two channels cannot word one fact differently.
